decisions.reason: Although its standalone page was no longer visible later, this adjustable quarter-pallet display is a core cardboard offering, so prior development and launch commitments make management inclined to keep it and read any weakness as temporary.

The pegboard-back cardboard display remains close to the established range, and despite reduced public visibility the firm is likely to justify earlier investment by continuing to offer it rather than withdrawing quickly.
As a standard quarter-pallet cardboard display at the center of the firm's business, it is the kind of product management would be most reluctant to drop after having launched and promoted it.
This eighth-pallet format is still a familiar extension of the core display line, so sunk costs and strategic fit support retaining it even if demand has been uneven.

With less fit to the firm's main cardboard specialization and weaker ongoing public commitment, the wooden display pallet is the most likely candidate to be discontinued so resources can return to core products and new development.
